subsystems.name: Momentum reservoir
subsystems.role: the mass that will be thrown past the planet to exchange momentum with it — in practice small icy bodies from the outer solar system, or bulk material launched from the Moon or a captured asteroid.

subsystems.name: Redirector
subsystems.role: steers each body onto a precisely phased encounter with the planet.

subsystems.name: Launcher
subsystems.role: the alternative to gravity assists: electromagnetic accelerators on a low-gravity body that fire projectiles past the planet.

subsystems.name: Dynamical control model
subsystems.role: predicts the cumulative effect of millions of encounters on every orbit in the system, well beyond the chaotic horizon of today's integrators.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: supplies the enormous continuous energy the campaign needs for hundreds of millions of years.
parts: space nuclear reactors or large solar arrays

subsystems.name: System watch
subsystems.role: watches the other planets, the asteroid belts and the planet's own moons for drift that the campaign might be causing.

buildSteps.title: Map the system with extreme precision
buildSteps.detail: Determine orbits, masses and the resonance structure well enough to model where they drift over hundreds of millions of years — today's integrations lose predictability after tens of millions of years because the system is chaotic.

buildSteps.title: Catalogue the momentum reservoir
buildSteps.detail: Find and characterise enough small bodies that their masses and orbits are known to the accuracy the encounter scheduling demands.

buildSteps.title: Prove momentum transfer at small scale
buildSteps.detail: Repeat kinetic-impactor and lander experiments on asteroids until a predicted change in a body's velocity can be delivered and then measured.

buildSteps.title: Build the redirector fleet
buildSteps.detail: Mass-produce autonomous spacecraft that can rendezvous with a body, land, and provide thrust or sail propulsion for years without ground control.

buildSteps.title: Nudge the first body into a phased encounter
buildSteps.detail: Send a small body through a close pass with the planet on the correct side and at the correct speed so that angular momentum is transferred — the planet moves outward a fraction of a millimetre to a metre.

buildSteps.title: Verify against the model
buildSteps.detail: Measure the planet's new orbital elements to the limit of tracking accuracy and confirm the change matches the control model before scaling up.

buildSteps.title: Ramp the encounter rate
buildSteps.detail: Increase the number of bodies handled per year until the outward drift equals the rate at which the habitable zone is receding — of order a few per cent of an astronomical unit each billion years.

buildSteps.title: Steer for the whole lifetime
buildSteps.detail: Continue for the Sun's remaining main-sequence life, while a permanent monitoring programme watches for resonance drift elsewhere in the system and corrects it.

prerequisites.why: the first deliberate change to a natural body's orbit was demonstrated in 2022; the energy delivered was a tiny fraction of what migration needs.

prerequisites.tech: Autonomous deep-space navigation and small-body rendezvous
prerequisites.why: a migration campaign involves millions of encounters that no ground team could fly.
the solar system is chaotic, so useful forecasts currently extend only tens of millions of years ahead.
the mass-driver variant must hurl bulk material at escape velocity continuously for geological time.

prerequisites.tech: Power sources in the thousands-of-terawatts class
prerequisites.why: raising a planet's orbit by a few per cent of an astronomical unit each billion years implies an average power of order thousands of terawatts, sustained.

prerequisites.tech: Institutions and automation that outlast civilisations
prerequisites.why: the campaign has no endpoint a single generation could see, so control has to be handed to something that keeps working unattended.

pathway.milestone: cataloguing of small bodies, and impact-deflection tests at the low end of the energy scale
pathway.unlocks: calibrated measurements of how momentum transfer really works on a natural body.

pathway.milestone: repeated, controlled nudging of one small asteroid's orbit and prediction of the result in advance
pathway.unlocks: confidence that encounter geometry can be scheduled rather than merely survived.

pathway.milestone: measurable migration of a moonlet or dwarf planet by a sustained campaign
pathway.unlocks: the control laws and resonance-management practice needed for a planet.

pathway.milestone: planet-scale migration begun, probably in parallel with a stellar sunshade that buys time immediately by lowering the insolation at the planet
pathway.unlocks: either sustained habitability far beyond the natural lifetime of the biosphere, or the failure modes that show the scheme is unworkable.

pathway.milestone: continuous operation across hundreds of millions of years
pathway.unlocks: a biosphere kept viable until the host star leaves the main sequence — the only window in which the project has any purpose.
